title: Tile roof, green awnings, a row of discs
label: Brand gallery
lede: Two freely licensed photographs: the first restaurant while it still carried the name, and one of the hundreds of buildings that outlived it. The drawings are our own. None of them reproduces the chain’s logo or its mascots.

archive.caption: The original restaurant at 216 West Cabrillo Boulevard, Santa Barbara, then the only one left.
archive.alt: A tile-roofed restaurant with green awnings, palm trees and a rooftop sign of round discs spelling Sambo’s

archive.caption: A former Sambo’s in Alpena, Michigan, operating as a Big Boy.
archive.alt: A low brick restaurant with a shingled roof and a Big Boy statue at the door
archive.credit: Photo: TenPoundHammer, cropped by Ubcule, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Big_Boy_former_Sambos_cropped.jpg), CC BY 2.0.

disclaimer: Colours were matched by eye to the 2005 photograph of the Santa Barbara restaurant, so they are approximate and describe that one building, not the chain’s 1970s signs. Sambo’s, Jolly Tiger, No Place Like Sam’s and Season’s were trademarks of their owners and are discussed here in historical and editorial context. The drawings are original illustrations and are not official assets.
